item.title: Florida Lemurs Aid Rainforest: Visitor encounters fund tree planting; link supports Madagascar
item.description: In North Florida, a wildlife center is now home to four red-ruffed lemurs, whose presence aids in funding crucial rainforest restoration projects in Madagascar. Visitor interactions facilitate the planting of thousands of trees each year. These critically endangered lemurs act as ambassadors for conservation, offering Florida visitors a unique opportunity to engage with essential forest preservation initiatives.

item.title: Belgium sank 23 concrete blocks in the North Sea to build world's first artificial energy island in a €7B project
item.description: Belgium is constructing the world's first artificial energy island in the North Sea. This massive structure will collect electricity from offshore wind farms and transmit it ashore. The island's design incorporates nature-inclusive elements to support marine life and bird species. While civil engineering nears completion, electrical infrastructure installation will continue until 2030. The project aims to become operational around 2030, enhancing European electricity exchange.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nearly 4,000 NYC students planted 100,000 plus beachgrass stalks to rebuild dunes and curb flooding
item.description: The National Wildlife Federation’s Resilient Schools and Communities programme has brought nearly 4,000 New York City public school students together to restore coastal dunes at Coney Island Creek Park. Since 2022, students, teachers and community members have planted more than 100,000 American beachgrass culms across 2.25 acres. The project aims to stabilise dunes, reduce erosion and build flood protection for more than 50,000 people living near the park.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Researchers turn water-treatment waste into a filter that removes up to 97.1% of microplastics
item.description: Researchers are investigating a new method to filter microplastics from water. This approach uses waste generated during water treatment as a filtering material. Tests show this repurposed waste achieved significant microplastic removal efficiencies. The innovative strategy tackles two environmental issues simultaneously. This circular approach could enhance water purification processes in the future.

item.title: Toxic air after 9/11: Mamdani releases documents showing how New Yorkers were misled
item.description: In a significant move, New York City disclosed withheld documents on air quality after 9/11, suggesting that officials may have misrepresented the dangers present post-collapse of the Twin Towers. A memo warned of potential lawsuits for toxic exposure and city liability concerns. There were also fears about asbestos levels and negative public response. This revelation follows a legal challenge from the advocacy group 9/11 Health Watch.

item.title: Roman cemetery dig reveals Stone Age man buried with 2 skulls, 42 teeth and an axe
item.description: In a startling archaeological find, researchers uncovered a burial site dating back to the Stone Age, predating nearby Roman graves by thousands of years. The grave contained a battle axe, striking amber beads, and a unique necklace fashioned from the teeth of 42 animals. Additionally, two human skulls were discovered alongside the skeleton, offering rare insights into the rituals and practices of ancient communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Napa Art Center Land Deal: di Rosa eases 162 acres into trust; future trail to Milliken Peak
item.description: A landmark conservation deal aims to safeguard a large portion of the di Rosa Center's Napa Valley landscape. Effectively shielding about 75% of the estate from future privatization, this agreement also secures vital financial resources for the center's ongoing operations. Exciting plans include a new public trail that will reach the summit of Milliken Peak, fostering an ideal mix of accessibility and artistic preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Copenhagen’s £200m underground museum opens in 2027 with dinosaurs, 14m specimens and eight galleries
item.description: Copenhagen’s new £200 million Natural History Museum will open on March 6, 2027, featuring eight immersive underground galleries and a collection of 14 million specimens. Visitors can explore dinosaur skeletons, 3D exhibits and the spectacular Ocean Hall, as the museum combines historic Botanical Garden buildings with striking new underground architecture inspired by nature.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian couple donate 187-acre Ontario island sanctuary after protecting its wildlife for 36 years
item.description: Jim and Anne Purvis bought 187.4 acres on Ontario’s Wilson Island in 1989 and spent 36 years protecting the land as a family sanctuary. They have now donated the property to the Northumberland Land Trust, ensuring its forests, wetlands, grasslands and habitats for species at risk remain protected as a permanent nature reserve.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AI Streamer Feud Escalates: N3on and Sneako trade insults; friendship rift over public criticism
item.description: N3on and Sneako’s friendship has taken a dramatic turn after Sneako publicly criticized N3on’s controversial AI streamer project. N3on, who announced an AI version of himself would stream 24/7 on Kick, accused Sneako of being disloyal and seeking views instead of addressing concerns privately. Sneako fired back with personal insults, while N3on defended the project and their friendship. The feud later intensified as both streamers continued trading jabs online.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Motorcyclist Startles IRL Stream: Security rushes in on La Piquiña; viewers debate robbery risk
item.description: Kick streamer La Piquiña experienced a frightening moment while livestreaming from the streets of Colombia at night. A motorcyclist suddenly approached his outdoor desktop setup, prompting concerns that a robbery could be underway. His nearby security team quickly intervened, and the rider left before the situation escalated. The encounter later sparked debate online, with fans praising the guards while others questioned the safety of streaming from an exposed public location after dark.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
